Goby: Whole mottled brown body, broad head and high eyes, two separate dorsals, rounded complete tail. The lower paired fin reads as a fan rather than a clearly fused suction disc; identity feature remains unresolved. No large detached paint seen; far paired fins are not independently resolved.
Blenny: Whole mottled body with a long continuous dorsal, blunt high-eyed head and complete rounded tail. Branched cirri above the eyes are conspicuous and possibly exaggerated into antler-like tufts. Lower fin roots overlap; far paired fins remain unresolved.
Wrasse: Whole green/orange scaled body and large fan pectoral, continuous dorsal and complete tail. Two projecting white teeth are exaggerated into rabbit-like incisors; record that identity concern. Lower fins overlap and the far pectoral is not clearly separate.
Damselfish: Deep oval blue body with dark vertical bars, continuous dorsal and complete forked tail. Near pectoral and two lower fin tips readable, far pectoral unresolved. No detached paint or obvious body cut in the original.
Clownfish: Three distinct white bands edged in black on orange: head, mid-body and tail stalk. Rounded fins and blunt snout read clearly; tail complete. Dorsal is deeply notched into two lobes and paired lower fins overlap; far pectoral unresolved. No detached paint seen.
Butterflyfish: Near-disc body, dark vertical bar through the eye and pointed tweezer snout are visible. Yellow/white body bands and rear dorsal eyespot also visible. Complete caudal tail, attached fins; several pointed extensions along the lower rear edge need anatomical/ownership review.
Surgeonfish: Oval grey/yellow-striped body, steep forehead, long dorsal and complete crescent tail. Caudal-peduncle spine is visible but enlarged into a conspicuous pale blade and needs anatomical review. Paired fin visibility incomplete; no detached body paint.
Angelfish: Separate marine replacement: rounded deep blue/yellow banded disc body, small mouth, visible small pale gill-cover spine, full caudal tail, trailing dorsal and anal tips. The broad pelvic fin is distinct from the original freshwater threadlike whips. Fin extensions remain exaggerated and paired far fins unresolved; species identity and anatomy still require the automatic owners. Original freshwater painting retained and refused.
Owl: Rounded facial disc and large forward-set eye, upright short-neck body, two separated leg shafts and feet. Folded wing and short tail overlap at their bases; far wing edge is not independently clear. No ear-like invented appendage or cropped toe.
Snowy Owl: Smooth round untufted head with yellow eye, white coat with dark bars and heavily feathered feet. Two feet visible with a gap between the lower legs; short complete tail lies below the folded wing. Wing/tail roots remain partly overlapped and need ownership review.
Roadrunner: Two complete separated legs and feet, streaked body, shaggy crest, heavy bill and full long tail are visible. The tail is cocked above the folded wing, departing from the requested wing-above-tail layout; preserve this observation for authoring review. No cropped terminal tip is apparent.
Sandgrouse: Plump body, small head, buff and black scalloped plumage, two short feathered legs and separate feet, and a continuous pointed tail are visible. The folded near wing ends before the tail tip but overlaps the tail root. Bill shape and root ownership need automatic identity/anatomy review.
Turkey: Standing non-display pose, folded barred tail, iridescent scale-like feathers, red wattles and snood, two fully separated legs and feet. Long dark breast beard could be mistaken for an appendage; preserve species identity during authoring. Folded wing overlaps the tail root but ends before its tip.
Woodpecker: Isolated standing pose without bark, black/white patterned body, red crest, chisel bill, two separated legs and gripping toes. Stiff pointed tail extends below and beyond the folded wing. Toe count/zygodactyl arrangement needs anatomy review; far wing root is not separately visible.
Guillemot: Dark brown upperparts and white belly, pointed bill, two separated legs and side-on feet. Folded wing is above the visible short tail and ends before its tip. Feet are painted as close parallel toes with webbing not clearly legible; tail appears relatively long and head/body profile needs identity review.
Eider Duck: Male black/white body with green nape, long wedge-shaped bill, two complete separated legs and feet. Short tail is visible behind the folded wing, with overlapping feather layers at the root. Webbing is not clearly legible in the side-on toes; standing proportions and feet need identity/anatomy review.
Coati: Four separated legs and feet, both ear tips, elongated upturned nose and a full erect ringed tail. Tail is clear of the torso. Ears are unusually pointed/large and silhouette is somewhat canid-like; identity review required.
Red Panda: Rust-red fur, white facial markings and ear margins, black belly/legs, and a complete ringed bushy tail. Four feet and both ear tips are separately visible. Upper far-leg roots overlap the body naturally; no cropped tip or extra limb apparent.
Pampas Fox: Grizzled grey back, buff sides, narrow muzzle, dark-tipped full bushy tail, four separated feet and both distinct ear tips. No cropped appendage apparent. Large ears and warm limb colour should be checked against canonical identity.
Striped Hyena: Distinct dark torso/leg stripes, erect dorsal mane, higher shoulders and lower rump, four separated feet and two ear tips. Tail tip is complete but lies close to the far hindleg. Mane spikes, lower foreleg fur points and close tail/hindleg ownership need author review.
Wildcat: Four distinct feet and both ear tips, grey-brown tabby striping, dark tail rings and a blunt black tail tip. Tail is complete and clear of the legs but rather short in projection; automatic identity/length review required. No extra limb apparent.
Black Bear: Black shaggy coat with tan muzzle, two rounded ear tips, four separate feet and a short visible tail protruding behind the rump. Far limb roots overlap the heavy torso; fine fur at shoulder/elbow remains an ownership concern. No cropped tip apparent.
Spectacled Bear: Cream facial rings and muzzle/chest markings on black shaggy fur; four complete separate feet, both ear tips, and a short visible tail. Far leg roots overlap the heavy torso, but no extra limb or cropped tip is apparent. Facial marking specificity and fine shoulder fur need review.
Hyrax: Compact rounded brown body, both rounded ear tips, four separated short legs and feet, blunt muzzle. No elongated tail is painted; a small rump nub is visible. Species-appropriate tail absence must be handled by the source-bound presence contract, not an invented long tail or inherited generic quadruped assumption. Toe/nail structure needs review.
